Industrial Growth and Worker Protest is a Duke dissertation from 1984 on North Carolina industrial labor. The Revolutionary Virginia author had already earned his Brown PhD in 1955 and was a William & Mary professor by 1970; these are separate doctoral careers.

The reviewer is John G. Selby, Roanoke's Duke-trained Civil War historian and author of Meade: The Price of Command. John Edward Selby was William & Mary's Revolutionary Virginia historian and died in 2001, before this 2006 review.

The publisher identifies Missionary Women's author as Rhonda A. Semple, assistant professor of history at the University of Northern British Columbia, matching the reviewer's institution and her work on British women's religious history.
